question.text: The image of an object placed in air formed by a convex refracting surface is at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> behind the surface. The image is real and is at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math> of the distance of the object from the surface. The wavelength of light inside the surface is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math> times the wavelength in air. The radius of the curved surface is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>13</mn></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>, the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ______ .
